classification: MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT over SYNTHETIC NONPROD FIXTURE DATA. Records how each required persona is represented today, distinguishing repository declaration from live nonprod. It is not a seed input, it provisions nothing and it grants nothing. No production data is described and no credential value appears.

enumerationMethod.statement: Six independent enumerations, unioned, each with an arithmetic residue check -- so a missed persona surfaces as an unaccounted row rather than as silence.

enumerations.name: Repository Employee declaration
enumerations.note: The complete declared Employee set. jobRoles[] = 12 keys; principals[] = 15 entries.

enumerations.name: Repository credential namespace
enumerations.note: Plus certificationEmailFor() for cw-emp-NNN, which is the FROZEN Certification world and out of scope by fence.

enumerations.name: Live employee-driven join
enumerations.source: SELECT over eos_workforce.employees LEFT JOIN eos_policy.employee_principal_links LEFT JOIN eos_policy.principals LEFT JOIN eos_policy.tenant_memberships, with a correlated role-key aggregate over user_role_assignments JOIN roles
enumerations.note: LEFT joins, so an Employee with no identity still appears.

enumerations.name: Live identity-driven complement
enumerations.note: So an identity with no Employee still appears. Found exactly one: the `owner`-Role Principal.

enumerations.name: Live Role-catalog sweep
enumerations.source: SELECT over all eos_policy.roles with active/total holder counts and role_capabilities counts
enumerations.note: So a persona-bearing Role with zero holders, or a held Role with zero capabilities, is visible.

residueChecks: Principals: 15 active-link + 14 revoked-link + 1 unlinked = 30 = SELECT count(*) FROM eos_policy.principals. No residue.
Employees: 15 linked + 2 unlinked = 17 = SELECT count(*) FROM eos_workforce.employees. No residue.
Role assignments: 40 active (attributed persona-by-persona) + 3 disabled zz_nonprod_acceptance = 43 = SELECT count(*) FROM eos_policy.user_role_assignments. No residue.
Memberships: 16 active + 14 disabled = 30; principals with no membership = 0. No residue.
Work eligibility: 7 rows, all open, each attributed to a named persona. Operational scopes: 6 rows, all open, each attributed. No residue.
Record assignments: 1 eos_ops.work_order_assignments row, attributed to P06; 0 eos_ops.reorder_request_assignments. No residue.
Every one of the 17 declared Employees appears either in a P-slot or in extraPersonasOutsideTargetPopulation.
enumerationMethod.howAMissedPersonaWouldSurface: As an eos_workforce.employees row with no P-slot and no extraPersonas entry; as a principal appearing in neither E4 nor E5 (structurally impossible -- they are exact complements); or as an active user_role_assignments row not attributable to a listed Principal, which the 40 + 3 = 43 residue check would fail.

classificationsSummary.countingRule: One count per (persona slot or fixture-staleness entry) x class. CREDENTIAL_CATALOG_DEFECT covers P01-P14 and P16 (15 slots; P15 makes no loader-key claim to be wrong about). INTENTIONAL_DENIAL counts P16 plus the two deliberately login-less Employees. WORK_ELIGIBILITY_DEFECT and OPERATIONAL_SCOPE_DEFECT are 0 because every live dimension row matches its fixture declaration and every withheld one is withheld deliberately. IDENTITY_DEFECT is 0 because all 16 firebase Principals resolve, all 15 links are active and single, and the dispatcher repair is verified. EXPERIENCE_NAV_DEFECT and WORKFLOW_AUTHORITY_DEFECT are 0 because they were NOT MEASURED, not because they are absent -- see measurementBlocked.

slotCoverage.note: P01 is VERIFIED because both halves were measured, not because it is correct -- see ownerAdminDrift. P02 is VERIFIED as a declared merge into P01, not as an independent persona. ZERO of the 13 verified slots is browser-login capable through the canonical credential loader.

registrationNote.question: Would an existing fixture-validation test cover this new fixture?
registrationNote.answer: NO. No test in functions/test/ globs functions/scripts/fixtures/; every consumer names its file explicitly, and functions/test/personaSuiteRegistration.test.mjs pins a hard-coded four-entry fixture list (personaAuthorityDimensions.v1.json, personaE2EScenarios.v1.json, sampleCompany.v2.json, syntheticNonprodWorkforceSeed.v1.json). This census is therefore not registration-blind: adding it to functions/package.json or to the two `paths:` blocks of .github/workflows/eos-admin-policy-tests.yml would register a path filter for a file no suite reads. Neither file was edited. If a future lane adds a validating suite for this census, BOTH `paths:` blocks and the npm script must be updated together, which is what personaSuiteRegistration.test.mjs enforces.
